cards.explanation: The answer is the hardness of their hearts. Paul says the ignorance is “…due to the hardness of their hearts.” The cause he names is the heart. Picture a cookie that sat in the oven way too long. You could hit it with a rolling pin and it would just laugh at you.
The answer is a craving for more. Paul says they've given themselves over “…with a craving for more.” That craving never says "okay, that's enough." It just asks again. I think this part is heavy.
The statement is true. Paul says it plainly: “But this is not the way you came to know Christ.” He's setting the believers' road next to the Gentiles' road, and they don't match.

The answer is the truth that is in Jesus. Paul says they were taught “…in keeping with the truth that is in Jesus…” The teaching lined up with Him. Think of a stamp that matches its cutter edge for edge. That's what it looks like when teaching and truth fit.
The answer is their old self. Paul says to put off “…your former way of life, your old self…” Two names for one thing, and both get taken off. That's step one in his three steps.

The answer is False. Paul doesn't call those desires honest. He calls them “deceitful.” The full line says the old self “…is being corrupted by its deceitful desires…” Honest desires would be easy to follow. Deceitful ones sound good while they're leading you off the counter.

The answer is minds. Paul says they were taught “…to be renewed in the spirit of your minds…” That's step two, and it happens in the mind. Taking off the old self is one move, and being renewed is another. Right here a lot of folks, me included, want to skip straight to the new apron.

The answer is God. Paul says the new self is “…created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.” The pattern is God Himself. That's a big step up from the old self. I can only say, wow, and then say it again, wow.

The reason is that we are all members of one another. Paul says to speak truthfully “…for we are all members of one another.” We're connected, so a lie to your neighbor is really a lie inside the family. It's like a team where one player lies about the score. Everybody ends up playing the wrong game.

The answer is False. The line is “Be angry, yet do not sin.” It doesn't forbid anger. It draws a line around what you do with it. I would've guessed "never," because I've burned a batch and I know how that goes.

The deadline is that the sun doesn't get to set on your anger. Paul says, “Do not let the sun set upon your anger…” That's the deadline, and it's short. Anger doesn't get to move in for the night. It has to be dealt with before the day is done.

The answer is devil. Paul says, “…and do not give the devil a foothold.” A foothold is a small place to stand. It's like a toe in the door. Paul's warning is to keep that door from being given even that much room.

The reason is to have something to share with the one in need. Paul says he must work, “…that he may have something to share with the one in need.” The work isn't just for himself. It ends up as something he can give. The text gives him a good reason to roll up his sleeves.

The answer is only what is helpful for building up. Paul says, “…but only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen.” Words are meant to build. That's a high bar for the mouth. I'm still working on it myself.
The statement is true. Paul says helpful talk is for “…bringing grace to those who listen.” So good words don't just sit there. They give something to the person hearing them.
The statement is true. The Holy Spirit is the one “…in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.” So the warning not to grieve Him comes with this reminder of what the believers have in Him.

The answer is just as in Christ God forgave them. Paul says to forgive each other “…just as in Christ God forgave you.” That's the pattern for it. We forgive the way we were forgiven. And honestly, friends, that makes holding a grudge look a lot smaller.
